narrative.overview: The portfolio feels like a working observatory rather than a sci-fi spectacle: technically precise, quietly confident, exploratory, and human. A deep-space canvas provides atmosphere while clear type, direct language, and conventional interaction patterns keep the hiring evidence easy to evaluate. The visual system earns identity through a small number of committed signals: orbital blue, sparse stellar motion, circular geometry around the portrait, and restrained module-like surfaces. The cosmic layer is environmental rather than ornamental; content stays calm and credible above it.
keyCharacteristics: Deep navy environment with cool blue navigational emphasis
Oversized, tightly set display type paired with highly legible body copy
Sparse circular and orbital motifs concentrated around identity moments
Soft tonal layering, fine borders, and restrained ambient lift
A responsive light mode that translates the identity into a subtle technical grid

rules.name: The Single Signal Rule
rules.body: Orbital Blue is the portfolio-wide action color. Timeline accents may identify individual roles, but they do not replace it for global navigation or calls to action.

rules.name: The Content Above Cosmos Rule
rules.body: Stellar colors belong to the atmospheric layer. Text and controls must always resolve to the core semantic palette for dependable contrast.

rules.name: The Scale Carries Identity Rule
rules.body: Keep Inter straightforward; create hierarchy through real changes in scale and weight, not gratuitous italics, serif cameos, or decorative effects.

rules.name: The Ambient, Not Floating Rule
rules.body: Shadows suggest light cast through the environment; borders and tonal shifts still define the structure.

rules.name: The Orbits Are Rare Rule
rules.body: Full circles mark identity, position, or status. Do not turn every container or icon into a floating bubble.

dos: Do keep professional evidence and calls to action visually clearer than the star field.
Do concentrate cosmic expression in the canvas, portrait orbit, section waypoints, and restrained ambient light.
Do use the responsive dark and light semantic palettes rather than hard-coding text colors inside components.
Do preserve generous body leading and bounded reading widths for fast recruiter scanning.
Do use job accent colors only within the experience timeline.
donts: Don't turn the interface into a literal spaceship dashboard or cover content with decorative telemetry.
Don't introduce generic developer-site tropes such as glowing code windows, floating technology logos, glass cards everywhere, or gratuitous gradients.
Don't use thick one-sided card borders as a default accent treatment.
Don't use bounce or elastic easing for navigational motion.
Don't let every surface become rounded, elevated, and independently framed; preserve hierarchy through grouping and negative space.
